mainTopic: Finishing תפילה, the כהן גדול's prayer and blood sprinklings, and what happened to the ארון
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of רבא, who walked backward when leaving his teacher רב יוסף, and רב יוסף blesses him. The גמרא compares this to finishing תפילה. A person takes three steps back, stays bowed, and then gives שלום first to God's right, which is his own left. Next it returns to the משנה and gives the words of the כהן גדול's short prayer on יום כיפור, which asks for a year of rain and plenty. A story about רבי חנינא בן דוסא shows that a truly righteous person's prayer is answered even against that request. A ברייתא then explains why the כהן גדול kept his prayer short: so the people would not fear he had died. A new משנה describes the אבן שתיה and the order of sprinkling the blood of the פר and the שעיר. The גמרא learns from the משנה's word 'ניטל' that it follows the view that the ארון was exiled to בבל. It contrasts this with the view that the ארון was hidden in its place, and begins עולא's conflicting report, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יוסף blesses רבא for honoring him
steps.stepSummary: People tell the blind רב יוסף that רבא walks backward when leaving him, and רב יוסף blesses רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told רב יוסף: 'This is what רבא does.' He said to him: 'May it be God's will that your head be raised over the whole city.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story. רבא would walk backward out of respect when leaving his teacher רב יוסף. Because רב יוסף was blind and could not see this, people told him, and he gave רבא a blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows how highly the חכמים valued a student who never turns his back on his רבי. The blessing that רבא's head would be raised over the city is a reward for this כבוד. This idea of leaving respectfully leads straight into the next topic, which is how to leave after תפילה.

phrases.english: They said to Rav Yosef:
phrases.notes: רב יוסף was blind and could not see what רבא was doing.

phrases.english: This is what Rava does.
phrases.notes: רבא walked backward when leaving his teacher.

phrases.english: He said to him: May it be (God's) will
that your head be raised over the entire city.
phrases.notes: Meaning: may you become the leader of the whole city.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְרַב יוֹסֵף הָכִי עָבֵיד רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story from the previous section about רבא's respect for רב יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student who leaves his teacher with great respect deserves a blessing of greatness.

steps.title: Three steps back after praying, then saying שלום
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that after תפילה a person steps back three steps and then says שלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלכסנדרי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: Someone who prays must take three steps backward, and after that say 'שלום'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule that connects to the story. Leaving God after תפילה is like leaving a teacher, so you step back respectfully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as רבא backed away from his רבי, a person finishing שמונה עשרה backs away from before the שכינה. The order matters. First you take the three steps, and only then do you 'give שלום', like saying goodbye.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of taking three steps back at the end of שמונה עשרה, which is still done today.

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri said
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One who prays must step
three steps backward,
and afterward give 'peace.'
phrases.notes: Like a farewell greeting when leaving the King.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic: leaving God after תפילה is compared to leaving one's teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After תפילה, take three steps back and then say שלום.

steps.title: Stay where you stepped and do not rush back
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי adds that after the three steps a person should stand in place, like a student who should not turn right back to his רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to him: Once he has stepped three steps back, he should stand there. It is like a student leaving his teacher: if he comes right back, he is like a dog that returns to its vomit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי adds a detail to the rule. After stepping back, you should not jump right back to your place. You stay standing where the steps brought you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stepping back is a respectful act of leaving. Undoing it right away makes it look like you never really took leave. The comparison to a dog returning to its vomit is harsh on purpose: going straight back spoils what you just did.

keyTerms.meaning: who takes leave of his teacher

phrases.english: Rav Mordekhai said to him:
Once he has stepped three steps backward —
there he should stand.
phrases.notes: He should not return to his original spot right away.

phrases.english: It is like a student who takes leave of his teacher;
if he returns immediately,
he is like a dog that returns to its vomit.
phrases.notes: This picture comes from the פסוק in משלי 26:11.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further detail to רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule. It does not argue with it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the three steps back, remain standing there and do not return immediately.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the three steps back
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule as רבי יהושע בן לוי and adds that without the steps it is as if one did not pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: Someone who prays must take three steps backward and then say 'שלום'. If he did not do so, it would have been better for him not to have prayed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא teaches the same rule. This backs up רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats the same rule word for word, which confirms it. It also adds how serious it is. Leaving the King without taking leave properly is so disrespectful that it would be better not to have prayed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)
it would be fitting for him / better for him

steps.confusionAlert: 'Better that he had not prayed' is strong language about how disrespectful this is. It does not mean the תפילה must necessarily be repeated.

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
One who prays must step
three steps backward
and afterward give 'peace,'
and if he did not do so,
it would have been fitting for him not to have prayed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a ברייתא for the rule in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule of three steps back, then שלום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording.

steps.title: שמעיה: say שלום to the right first, then the left
steps.stepSummary: In the name of שמעיה: the שלום is given first to the right and then to the left, proven from two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of שמעיה they said: He gives 'שלום' to the right and then to the left. As it says: 'From His right hand, a fiery law for them.' And it also says: 'A thousand will fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with another detail: which side to turn to first when saying שלום. Two פסוקים are brought as proof that the right side comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows that God gave the תורה with His right hand, so the right side is important. The second פסוק is added with 'ואומר' ('and it also says'). Why a second proof is needed is the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and it also says' — introduces a second פסוק

phrases.english: And in the name of Shemaya they said:
that he gives 'peace' to the right,
and afterward to the left,
as it is said: 'From His right hand, a fiery law for them,'
phrases.notes: דברים 33:2

phrases.english: and it says: 'A thousand will fall at your side,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 91:7

phrases.english: 'and ten thousand at your right.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם שְׁמַעְיָה אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further detail about how to give the שלום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When saying שלום at the end of תפילה, turn first to the right, then to the left.

steps.title: Why bring a second verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed 'ואומר', a second פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it also says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a second פסוק was needed when the first already mentions the right hand. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a source brings two proofs, the גמרא assumes the first one alone was not enough. The task now is to find what was missing in the first פסוק.

phrases.english: What is (the need for) 'and it says'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי וְאוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the structure of the proof in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first פסוק was not enough on its own.

steps.title: The first verse might just reflect normal habit
steps.stepSummary: The first פסוק could be read as simply describing the normal habit of giving with the right hand. The second פסוק shows that the right side is truly more important.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you might say it is just the normal way to give with the right hand, come and hear: 'A thousand will fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The first פסוק alone might only describe the usual habit, so the second פסוק is needed to prove that the right side is more important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving the תורה 'from His right hand' could just be the normal way anyone hands something over. It would not prove that the right side is special. In the second פסוק, ten thousand fall at the right compared to one thousand at the side, which shows that the right side is more important. So we turn to the right first.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say (a possible objection)

steps.whatToRemember: Finish תפילה by taking three steps back, then say שלום first to the right, then to the left. Stay standing there and do not rush back. The right side comes first because it is truly more important, as the second פסוק shows. It is not just a habit.

phrases.english: And if you would say it is the normal way of things
to give with the right hand,
come and hear:
'A thousand will fall at your side,'
'and ten thousand at your right.'
phrases.notes: The right is linked with the larger number, so it is the more important side.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא אוֹרְחָא דְמִילְּתָא הִיא לְמִיתַּב בְּיָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first פסוק might only show a normal habit of giving with the right hand. The second פסוק proves that the right side is truly more important.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The right side is truly more important, so שלום is given to the right first.

steps.title: רבא corrects אביי about which side is 'right'
steps.stepSummary: רבא sees אביי giving שלום to his own right first. He explains that 'right' means the right of הקדוש ברוך הוא, which is the person's own left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא saw אביי giving שלום to his right side first. He said to him: Do you think I meant your right? I mean your left, which is the right of הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.whatsHappening: A short story shows how the rule from שמעיה (give שלום to the right first) is actually carried out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that the right side comes first. But he explains that it means God's right. Since one stands facing the שכינה, God's right is opposite one's own left. So a person bows to his own left first.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving שלום, meaning bowing to the side at the end of תפילה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא argues with the rule 'right first.' He keeps the rule. He only explains that 'right' means God's right, which is your own left, because you are facing Him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of bowing to the left first when saying עושה שלום at the end of שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: Rava saw Abaye
giving 'peace' to the right first

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי סָבְרַתְּ לִימִין דִּידָךְ?
phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think I meant your right?
I am talking about your left,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוֵי יְמִינוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
phrases.english: which is the right of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
phrases.notes: Facing God, His right is opposite your left.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ לִימִין דִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of 'right first' from steps 5 and 7, and defines which right is meant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Give שלום first to God's right, which is the person's own left.

steps.title: אביי and רבא took the three steps in one bow
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב הונא reports that he saw אביי and רבא take all three steps while staying bowed the whole time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בריה דרב הונא said: I saw אביי and רבא take three steps in one bow.
steps.whatsHappening: Another eyewitness report that shows how the three steps back are done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three steps are not done standing up straight. אביי and רבא stayed bowed through all three steps without straightening in between. This shows humility before God.

keyTerms.meaning: Three steps back at the end of תפילה

steps.whatToRemember: End of the section on finishing תפילה: take three steps back, stay bowed throughout, then give שלום to your own left (God's right) first and then to your right.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chiya son of Rav Huna said:
I saw Abaye and Rava
that they took three steps
in one bow.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְאַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more practical detail about the three steps discussed earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three steps are taken while staying bowed the whole time.

steps.title: What was the כהן גדול's short prayer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says the כהן גדול says a short prayer in the outer chamber, and asks what he prayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And he prays a short prayer in the outer chamber.' What did he pray?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and sets up the next step by asking for the words of the כהן גדול's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור, after leaving the קודש הקדשים, the כהן גדול prays in the היכל, the outer room. The משנה only says the prayer was short. It does not give the words, so the גמרא asks for them.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer chamber, the היכל, outside the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: 'And he prays a short prayer'
'in the outer chamber.'
What does he pray?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מְצַלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא leaves the laws of finishing תפילה and goes back to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual words of the כהן גדול's short prayer.

steps.title: The prayer: a rainy and hot year
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רב: the כהן גדול asked that the coming year be rainy and hot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב אדא and רבין בר רב אדא both said in the name of רב: 'May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that this year be rainy and hot.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving the opening words of the כהן גדול's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer asks for a year that is good for crops. Two brothers report the same wording from רב. The word 'hot' will be questioned in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא בַּר רַב אַדָּא וְרָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Adda and Ravin bar Rav Adda
both said in the name of Rav:
May it be Your will, Lord our God,
that this year be rainy and hot.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He prayed that the year be rainy and hot.

steps.title: Is heat a good thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why anyone would pray for heat, since heat is not a blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is heat a good thing?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the prayer it was just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Too much heat can dry out and ruin crops. So asking for a 'hot' year does not seem to make sense in a prayer for blessing.

phrases.english: Is heat a good thing?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחוּנָה מְעַלְּיוּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks one word in the prayer quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'ושחונה' (and hot) in the prayer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Heat harms crops, so it should not be something one asks for.

steps.title: Corrected wording: if hot, let it be rainy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: the prayer is that if the year is hot, it should also be rainy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: 'If it is hot, may it be rainy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing how the prayer should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול does not ask for heat. He asks that if the year turns out hot, enough rain will come so the heat does not ruin the crops.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (a correction of the wording)

phrases.english: Rather, say:
If it is hot, may it be rainy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The prayer seemed to ask for heat as a blessing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prayer asks that a hot year should still have rain.

steps.title: רב אחא adds the ending of the prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא, in the name of רב יהודה, adds three more requests: kingship should stay with יהודה, Jews should not need each other for a living, and travelers' prayers against rain should not be accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרבא finished the prayer in the name of רב יהודה: 'May ruling power not leave the house of יהודה; may Your nation ישראל not need each other for their living; and may the prayer of travelers not come before You.'
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds more lines to the end of the כהן גדול's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added requests ask for leadership to stay with יהודה and for a good harvest so no one depends on others. The last line asks God not to accept travelers who pray for the rain to stop just for their own comfort, since the world needs rain.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava finished it
in the name of Rav Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: לָא יִעְדֵּי עָבֵיד שׁוּלְטָן מִדְּבֵית יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: May ruling power not leave the house of Judah,
and may Your nation Israel not be
in need of a living from one another,
and may there not enter before You
the prayer of travelers.
phrases.notes: Travelers who ask for the rain to stop.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מְסַיֵּים בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the ending to the prayer given in steps 11 and 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prayer also includes requests for kingship of יהודה, a living for ישראל, and that travelers' prayers against rain not be accepted.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayers stop and start the rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן דוסא was caught in the rain on the road and prayed, and it stopped. When he got home he prayed again, and the rain came back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן דוסא was walking on the road. Rain fell on him. He said: 'Master of the world! The whole world is comfortable, and חנינא is suffering.' The rain stopped. When he came home he said: 'Master of the world! The whole world is suffering, and חנינא is comfortable.' The rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a traveler whose prayer against rain was answered, linking to the last line of the כהן גדול's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול prayed that travelers' prayers against rain should not be accepted. Yet רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayer worked anyway. And as soon as he was home, he asked for the rain to return for everyone else.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא הֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל בְּאוֹרְחָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa was walking on the road.
Rain fell on him. He said:
Master of the world!

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ בְּנַחַת, וַחֲנִינָא בְּצַעַר.
phrases.english: The whole world is comfortable, and Chanina is suffering.
The rain stopped.
When he came to his house, he said:
Master of the world!

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ בְּצַעַר, וַחֲנִינָא בְּנַחַת.
phrases.english: The whole world is suffering, and Chanina is comfortable.
The rain came.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא הֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the line about travelers' prayers in step 14 with a story where such a prayer was answered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prayers of רבי חנינא בן דוסא were answered immediately, both to stop the rain and to bring it back.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the כהן גדול's prayer could not override רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the כהן גדול's prayer did not help against the prayer of רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What did the prayer of the כהן גדול accomplish against רבי חנינא בן דוסא?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the lesson of the story and closes the topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול prayed on the holiest day, right after his service in the קודש הקדשים, that travelers' prayers not be accepted. Still, God answered רבי חנינא בן דוסא. This shows how great his holiness was, since God did what he asked.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול's short prayer asks for a good year of rain and plenty. But the prayer of a truly righteous person like רבי חנינא בן דוסא is answered even against it.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ צְלוֹתֵיהּ דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: What did the prayer of the High Priest help
against Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ צְלוֹתֵיהּ דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the story in step 15, connecting it back to the prayer in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The holiness of רבי חנינא בן דוסא was so great that even the כהן גדול's prayer on יום כיפור could not block his request.

steps.title: A כהן גדול who prayed too long
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a כהן גדול who made his prayer long. The other כהנים got worried and decided to go in after him. Just as they started to enter, he came out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There once was a כהן גדול who made his prayer long. His fellow כהנים voted to go in after him. Just as they began to go in, he came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא story connected to the משנה's rule that the כהן גדול kept his prayer short. This step sets up the scene for the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other כהנים feared that something bad had happened to him inside, so they planned to go in and check. The story shows in real life why a long prayer is a problem: it scares people.

keyTerms.meaning: A story / an incident that happened

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was an incident with a certain High Priest
who made his prayer long,
and his fellow priests voted
to go in after him.
phrases.notes: They were worried he had died or fainted.

phrases.english: They began to go in
and he was coming out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story of רבי חנינא בן דוסא to the משנה's rule that the כהן גדול's prayer was short.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story is told of a כהן גדול whose long prayer worried the other כהנים.

steps.title: The priests ask why he prayed so long
steps.stepSummary: The other כהנים ask the כהן גדול why he made his prayer long.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Why did you make your prayer long?
steps.whatsHappening: The כהנים ask him to explain himself. This question sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not just curiosity. It hints that he did something unusual that went against the normal practice.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי מָה הֶאֱרַכְתָּ בִּתְפִלָּתֶךָ?
phrases.english: They said to him: Why did you make your prayer long?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי מָה הֶאֱרַכְתָּ בִּתְפִלָּתֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The כהנים question the כהן גדול after he comes out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the כהן גדול made his prayer long.

steps.title: He answers that he was praying for them and the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול says he was praying for them and for the בית המקדש, that it should not be destroyed. Why should that bother them?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Does it bother you that I prayed for you and for the בית המקדש, that it should not be destroyed?
steps.whatsHappening: The כהן גדול defends his long prayer by explaining what he was praying for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that the content of his prayer was so important that it was worth the extra time. He answers with a question, as if to say the long prayer was obviously a good thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it hard in your eyes? / Does it bother you?

phrases.english: He said to them: Is it troubling in your eyes
that I prayed for you
and for the Temple, that it should not be destroyed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: קָשֶׁה בְּעֵינֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כהנים' question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He prayed long because he was praying for the כהנים and for the בית המקדש not to be destroyed.

steps.title: The priests tell him not to make it a habit
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים tell him not to get used to doing this. They quote the משנה, which says the כהן גדול does not make his prayer long so as not to frighten ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Don't make a habit of doing this. We learned in the משנה: He would not make his prayer long, so as not to frighten the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The כהנים close the story by reminding him of the rule in the משנה and the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a very good prayer must not be stretched out here, because the people waiting outside might think the כהן גדול died in קודש הקדשים. Worry for the people's feelings outweighs making the prayer longer. This ties the story back to the משנה's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not make it a habit

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול keeps his prayer short on יום הכיפורים so that the people do not panic and fear he died inside.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that care for the community's peace of mind can set limits even on holy prayer.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַל תְּהִי רָגִיל לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן,
phrases.english: They said to him: Do not make a habit of doing so,
for we learned:
He would not make his prayer long
so as not to frighten the Jewish people.
phrases.notes: They might fear he had died inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַל תְּהִי רָגִיל לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן, שֶׁהֲרֵי שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the כהן גדול's defense by citing the משנה's rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The prayer must stay short so as not to frighten ישראל, as the משנה taught.

steps.title: New משנה: the אבן שתיה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. After the ארון was gone, there was a rock in קודש הקדשים from the time of the early נביאים. It was called the אבן שתיה. It stood three finger-widths above the ground, and the כהן גדול placed the קטורת on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: After the ארון was taken away, there was a stone there from the days of the early prophets, and it was called 'שתיה'. It was three finger-widths higher than the ground, and he would place the קטורת on it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It explains where the כהן גדול put the קטורת in the second בית המקדש, when there was no ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first בית המקדש the קטורת was placed between the poles of the ארון. Once the ארון was gone, the אבן שתיה took its place as the spot where he set it down.

keyTerms.meaning: The early prophets (like דוד and שמואל)

steps.confusionAlert: 'נוֹתֵן' here means placing the pan of קטורת. The blood was not placed on this stone.

phrases.english: MISHNA: After the Ark was taken away,
there was a stone there
from the days of the early prophets,
and it was called 'Foundation',
three finger-widths higher than the ground,
and on it he would place the incense.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִשֶּׁנִּיטַּל אָרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה continuing the יום הכיפורים service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without the ארון, the קטורת was placed on the אבן שתיה.

steps.title: Sprinkling the bull's blood: one up, seven down
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול takes the פר's blood from the כהן who was stirring it. He goes back into קודש הקדשים to the same spot and sprinkles once upward and seven times downward.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took the blood from the one who was stirring it. He went into the place he had gone into before, stood where he had stood before, and sprinkled from it once upward and seven times downward.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the next part of the service, sprinkling the blood of the פר inside קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood had to be stirred so it would not thicken while he was busy with the קטורת. He returns to exactly the same place as before and does eight sprinklings: one 'up' and seven 'down'.

keyTerms.meaning: Stirring (the blood, so it won't thicken)

phrases.english: He took the blood
phrases.notes: The blood of the bull.

phrases.english: from the one who was stirring it,
he entered the place where he had entered,
phrases.notes: קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: and stood in the place where he had stood,
and sprinkled from it
once upward and seven times downward.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָטַל אֶת הַדָּם מִמִּי שֶׁהָיָה מְמָרֵס בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the קטורת to the blood of the פר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פר's blood is sprinkled in קודש הקדשים once upward and seven times downward.

steps.title: How he sprinkled and counted, then set the bowl down
steps.stepSummary: He did not aim up or down. He flicked like someone swinging a whip. He counted 'one, one and one, one and two...' up to 'one and seven'. Then he went out and put the bowl on the golden stand in the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not aim to sprinkle up or down, but like one who whips. This is how he counted: one; one and one; one and two; one and three; one and four; one and five; one and six; one and seven. He went out and placed it on the golden stand in the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the exact way of sprinkling and counting, and where the leftover blood was put.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Up' and 'down' does not mean he aimed at the ceiling or the floor. It describes the movement of his hand, like a whip. He repeats 'one' with each number so he won't confuse the first upward sprinkle with the downward ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who whips (a flicking motion)
The Sanctuary (the room outside קודש הקדשים)

steps.confusionAlert: 'One and two' does not mean three sprinklings. It means the upward one plus the second downward one, counted together so he won't lose track.

phrases.english: And he did not intend to sprinkle
neither upward nor downward
but like one who whips.
And this is how he would count:
One; one and one;
one and two; one and three;
one and four; one and five;
one and six; one and seven.
He went out and placed it
on the golden stand in the Sanctuary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא הָיָה מִתְכַּוֵּון לְהַזּוֹת לֹא לְמַעְלָה וְלֹא לְמַטָּה אֶלָּא כְּמַצְלִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the sprinkling from the previous step was done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He sprinkles with a whip-like motion and counts with 'one' repeated each time, then puts the bowl on the golden stand.

steps.title: The same procedure with the goat's blood
steps.stepSummary: They bring the שעיר. He slaughters it, catches its blood in a bowl, goes into קודש הקדשים, and sprinkles once up and seven down, counting the same way. Then he puts the bowl on the second golden stand in the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought him the goat. He slaughtered it and caught its blood in a bowl. He entered where he had entered, stood where he had stood, and sprinkled once upward and seven times downward. He counted: one; one and one; one and two, etc. He went out and placed it on the second golden stand in the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the whole sprinkling process, this time with the blood of the שעיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything matches the פר's service, with one difference: this bowl goes on a second stand. That detail sets up רבי יהודה's disagreement in the next step.

phrases.english: They brought him the goat,
he slaughtered it and received its blood in a bowl,
he entered the place where he had entered,
and stood in the place where he had stood,
and sprinkled from it
once upward and seven times downward,
and this is how he would count:

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת, אַחַת וְאַחַת, אַחַת וּשְׁתַּיִם וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: one; one and one; one and two; etc.
He went out and placed it
on the second golden stand in the Sanctuary.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ אֶת הַשָּׂעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the פר's sprinkling procedure for the שעיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שעיר's blood is sprinkled the same way and placed on a second golden stand.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: there was only one stand
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees and says there was only one stand. So the כהן גדול lifted off the פר's blood and put the שעיר's blood in its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: There was only one stand there. He took the bull's blood and placed the goat's blood...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues on the detail of a 'second stand' and explains how one stand was enough. The משנה continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view, the תנא קמא, holds that there were two stands so the bowls could not get mixed up. רבי יהודה says there was one stand, and the bowls were swapped: the פר's blood came off and the שעיר's blood went on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
There was not there
anything but one stand alone.
He took the bull's blood
and placed the goat's blood,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues next.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָיָה שָׁם אֶלָּא כֵּן אֶחָד בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the 'second golden stand' mentioned in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה there was one stand, and the פר's blood was removed so the שעיר's blood could be placed there.

steps.title: Sprinkling the bull's blood on the curtain from outside
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול sprinkles the פר's blood on the outside of the פרוכת, facing where the ארון is: once upward and seven times downward, counting the same way as before.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sprinkled from it on the curtain opposite the Ark, from outside: once upward and seven times downward. He did not aim, etc. And this is how he counted, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the order of the service. Now the כהן גדול is outside קודש הקדשים, in the היכל, and sprinkles the פר's blood on the curtain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the sprinklings were inside קודש הקדשים. This is a new set of sprinklings in a new place: on the פרוכת, from the היכל side. The 'etc.' tells us the method and the counting are the same as the inside sprinklings described in step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: The curtain separating the היכל from קודש הקדשים
Opposite (facing) the place of the Ark
From outside, meaning from the היכל side

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with steps 22–24. Those sprinklings were INSIDE קודש הקדשים. These are on the curtain, from OUTSIDE.

phrases.english: And he sprinkled from it on the curtain
phrases.notes: 'From it' means from the bull's blood, which he picks up again from the stand

phrases.english: that is opposite the Ark, from outside,
once upward and seven times downward
and he did not aim, etc.
phrases.notes: Refers back to the whip-like motion from step 23

phrases.english: And this is how he would count, etc.
phrases.notes: 'One, one and one, one and two...'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִזָּה מִמֶּנּוּ עַל הַפָּרוֹכֶת שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הָאָרוֹן מִבַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's order of the service after both bloods were placed on the stands
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פר's blood is sprinkled on the outside of the פרוכת, once up and seven down, with the same counting method

steps.title: Sprinkling the goat's blood on the curtain from outside
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול swaps the bowls: he picks up the שעיר's blood and puts down the פר's blood. Then he sprinkles the שעיר's blood on the פרוכת the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took the goat's blood and put down the bull's blood, and sprinkled from it on the curtain opposite the Ark, from outside: once upward and seven times downward, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the curtain sprinkling, this time with the שעיר's blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is the same as inside: first the פר, then the שעיר. The swap of bowls fits רבי יהודה's view from step 25, that there was only one stand, so one bowl had to come off before the other was put down.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the rest is the same as before

phrases.english: He took the goat's blood
and put down the bull's blood,
phrases.notes: He puts it on the stand in place of the goat's blood

phrases.english: and sprinkled from it on the curtain
that is opposite the Ark, from outside,
once upward and seven times downward, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָטַל דַּם הַשָּׂעִיר וְהִנִּיחַ דַּם הַפָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the curtain sprinkling of step 26, now with the goat's blood
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the פר, the שעיר's blood is sprinkled on the פרוכת the same way

steps.title: Mixing the bull's blood and the goat's blood
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול pours the פר's blood into the שעיר's blood. Then he pours the full bowl into the empty one so the bloods mix well.
steps.simpleTranslation: He poured the bull's blood into the goat's blood, and he put the full bowl into the empty one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes how the two bloods are combined after the curtain sprinklings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring once is not enough to mix them fully. So he pours the combined blood from the full bowl back into the empty bowl, and the blood is mixed well. This mixture is used next for the golden מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: עֵירָה דַּם הַפָּר לְתוֹךְ דַּם הַשָּׂעִיר,
phrases.english: He poured the bull's blood into the goat's blood,
and put the full bowl into the empty one.
phrases.notes: Pouring back and forth so the bloods mix completely

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵירָה דַּם הַפָּר לְתוֹךְ דַּם הַשָּׂעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next stage after both curtain sprinklings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two bloods are poured together and then poured again into the empty bowl to mix them fully
steps.whatToRemember: Order of the blood sprinklings: פר inside, שעיר inside, פר on the פרוכת, שעיר on the פרוכת, then mix the two bloods.

steps.title: The משנה's word 'taken' shows the ארון went to בבל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the משנה (step 21) said the ארון was 'taken,' not 'hidden away.' So the משנה follows the view that the ארון was exiled to בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not teach 'after it was hidden away,' but 'after it was taken.' We learned the משנה like the one who says the Ark was exiled to Babylon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It reads closely one word in the משנה from step 21 and draws a conclusion about which opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a famous dispute: did the ארון go to בבל, or was it hidden in the בית המקדש? 'Hidden' (נגנז) would point to the hiding view. 'Taken' (ניטל) sounds like it was carried away, so the משנה follows the exile view. The next step brings the source for that view.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים on the משנה
Was hidden away (stored out of sight)
We learned (the משנה) like the one who says

steps.confusionAlert: The word being analyzed is not here. It comes from step 21: 'משניטל ארון,' 'after the Ark was taken.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic גמרא move: one word in the משנה tells us which side of a dispute the משנה follows.

phrases.english: Gemara
It does not teach 'after it was hidden away,'
but 'after it was taken.'
We learned it like the one who says
the Ark was exiled to Babylon.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״מִשֶּׁנִּגְנַז״ לָא קָתָנֵי, אֶלָּא ״מִשֶּׁנִּיטַּל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the order of the service and goes back to analyze the opening line of the משנה (step 21)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's word ניטל shows it follows the view that the ארון was exiled to בבל

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: The ארון was exiled to בבל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says the ארון went to בבל. His proof is a פסוק saying נבוכדנאצר brought 'the precious vessels of the House of ה׳' to בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says: The Ark was exiled to Babylon, as it says: 'And at the turn of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, with the precious vessels of the House of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the view it just mentioned. It shows that there really is a תנא who holds the ארון was exiled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reads 'precious vessels of the House of ה׳' as including the ארון, since it was the most precious vessel of all. So the ארון went with them to בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: King of בבל who destroyed the first בית המקדש

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The Ark was exiled to Babylon, as it says:
'And at the turn of the year
King Nebuchadnezzar sent
and brought him to Babylon
phrases.notes: 'Him' means King Yehoyachin

phrases.english: with the precious vessels of the House of ה׳.'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב לו:י. The most precious vessel is the Ark.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אָרוֹן גָּלָה לְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the view named in step 29
steps.raayaObject: That there is a תנא who holds the ארון was exiled to בבל, so the משנה can follow him
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אליעזר, who reads 'כלי חמדת בית ה׳' as including the ארון

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: The ארון was exiled, from 'nothing will be left'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי also says the ארון went to בבל. He reads 'לא יותר דבר' (nothing will be left) as hinting to the דברות, the Ten Commandments inside the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says: The ארון was exiled to בבל, as it says: 'Nothing shall be left, says ה׳.' These are the עשרת הדברות that are in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second תנא who agrees that the ארון was exiled, using a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיה says everything in the king's house will be carried to בבל and 'לא יותר דבר.' רשב"י connects the word דבר to the דברות, the לוחות with the Ten Commandments. Since the לוחות were inside the ארון, the ארון went to בבל too.

keyTerms.meaning: A thing; here read as a hint to the דברות
That are in it (inside the ארון)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is a wordplay: דָּבָר ('a thing') sounds like דִּבְּרוֹת ('commandments'). It is not the plain meaning of the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
The Ark was exiled to Babylon, as it says:
'Nothing shall be left, says ה׳' —
phrases.notes: ישעיה לט:ו

phrases.english: these are the Ten Commandments that are in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר: אָרוֹן גָּלָה לְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second תנא in the same ברייתא who agrees with רבי אליעזר, with a different פסוק
steps.raayaObject: That the ארון was exiled to בבל
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיה לט:ו, reading דבר as a hint to the דברות inside the ארון

steps.title: רבי יהודה: The ארון was hidden in its place
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה (בן לקיש) disagrees. He holds the ארון was hidden in its own place, because the פסוק says its poles are there 'until this day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה (בן לקיש) says: The ארון was hidden in its place, as it says: 'And the ends of the poles were seen from the holy place, in front of the inner sanctuary, but they were not seen outside; and they are there until this day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposing view: the ארון never left. It was hidden away where it was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the ארון's poles 'are there until this day.' Since the פסוק can be read at any time in history, 'until this day' means forever. So the ארון must still be there, hidden. This is the view the משנה did NOT follow, since it said 'ניטל' and not 'נגנז.'

keyTerms.meaning: Was hidden away in its place
The poles used to carry the ארון
Until this day; read here as 'forever'

steps.whatToRemember: Two views on the ארון: רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי say it was exiled to בבל. רבי יהודה (בן לקיש) says it was hidden in its place. The משנה's word 'ניטל' fits the exile view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the dispute about the hidden ארון, which the גמרא continues to discuss after this point.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda (ben Lakish) says:
phrases.notes: Some versions call him רבי יהודה בן לקיש, and others leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: The Ark was hidden in its place, as it says:
'And the ends of the poles were seen from the holy place
phrases.notes: מלכים א ח:ח

phrases.english: in front of the inner sanctuary
but they were not seen outside;
and they are there until this day.'
phrases.notes: 'Until this day' = forever, so the Ark is still hidden there

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה (בֶּן לָקִישׁ) אוֹמֵר: אָרוֹן בִּמְקוֹמוֹ נִגְנַז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing view in the same ברייתא, against רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ארון was not exiled. It was hidden in its place, based on 'ויהיו שם עד היום הזה'

steps.title: This view conflicts with עולא's report
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא remarks that the earlier report of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's view (that the ארון went to בבל) conflicts with something עולא reported.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with עולא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a short comment. The view just quoted does not match what עולא reported. This line is a setup: next the גמרא will bring עולא's story to show the conflict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 31, a ברייתא quoted רבי שמעון בן יוחאי as saying the ארון went to בבל. עולא tells a story about רבי שמעון בן יוחאי that points the other way, so the two reports cannot both be right. The גמרא flags this before telling the story.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees with / conflicts with

steps.confusionAlert: Read 'ופליגא דעולא' as 'this view conflicts with what עולא reported.' It does not mean עולא is arguing on his own. As the full story on the next עמוד shows, the clash is over what רבי שמעון בן יוחאי himself held.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Ulla.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the view reported earlier in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי clashes with a different report brought by עולא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The view that the ארון was exiled to בבל, as reported in the ברייתא, does not match עולא's report.

steps.title: עולא's story: a question asked in Rome
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports that רבי מתיא בן חרש asked רבי שמעון בן יוחאי in Rome a question. It starts from the fact that רבי אליעזר taught twice that the ארון went to בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: רבי מתיא בן חרש asked רבי שמעון בן יוחאי in Rome: 'Since רבי אליעזר taught us once and a second time that the ארון was exiled to בבל...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings עולא's story, which is the source of the conflict. רבי מתיא בן חרש begins a question to רבי שמעון בן יוחאי by quoting רבי אליעזר's view, which is backed by two proofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Once and a second time' means רבי אליעזר proved his point from two separate פסוקים. The question is building toward asking רבי שמעון בן יוחאי for his own opinion. That is where the contrast with step 31 will appear.

keyTerms.meaning: A first and a second time, meaning from two separate פסוקים

phrases.english: As Ulla said:
Rabbi Matya ben Ḥarash asked

phrases.aramaic: אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי בְּרוֹמִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai in Rome:
And since Rabbi Eliezer teaches us
a first time and a second time,
that the Ark was exiled to Babylonia,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא, שָׁאַל רַבִּי מַתְיָא בֶּן חָרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the actual story from עולא that step 33 referred to.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a conflicting report of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's view about the ארון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's report of the conversation in Rome between רבי מתיא בן חרש and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.

steps.title: Naming רבי אליעזר's two פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא interrupts the story to identify רבי אליעזר's two proofs. The first is the פסוק already quoted. It then asks what the second one is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first is the one we already said: 'And he brought him to בבל, along with the precious vessels of the House of ה׳.' What is the second?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes a short break from the story to explain 'a first and a second time.' It points back to the first פסוק and asks which פסוק is the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first proof was already brought in step 30: the 'precious vessels' brought to בבל include the ארון. The second proof has not been mentioned yet, so the גמרא asks for it.

phrases.english: The first is that which we said:
"And brought him to Babylonia
along with the precious vessels of the House of the Lord";
what is the second?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנִיָּה מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the phrase 'a first and a second time' from the story by identifying the first פסוק and asking for the second.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק is רבי אליעזר's second proof that the ארון went to בבל?

steps.title: The second פסוק: 'ויצא מבת ציון'
steps.stepSummary: The second proof is the פסוק 'And gone from the daughter of Zion is...'. It continues past the end of this passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And gone from the daughter of Zion is...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by beginning to quote the second פסוק, from איכה. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'gone from the daughter of Zion' describe something leaving ירושלים. The next part of the פסוק ('all her splendor') will be read as a hint to the ארון. This is the second time רבי אליעזר shows the ארון left for בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: And gone from the daughter of Zion is (איכה א:ו)

phrases.english: As it is written: "And gone from the daughter of Zion is

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיֵּצֵא מִבַּת צִיּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35 by giving the second פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second proof is the פסוק in איכה, 'ויצא מבת ציון...'. It continues on the next amud.
